hypotheses.reasoning: audit-consumer v1.27.6 processes audit.events in batches. At offset 618947 it hits msg-750657, and expandReferences throws RangeError: call stack overflow (likely a deeply nested or self-referencing payload). The process crashes with FATAL and exits with code 1. On each restart the consumer resumes at the committed offset 618947, which was never advanced past the bad message, so it re-reads msg-750657 and crashes again. That produces the CrashLoopBackOff, and the audit.events lag grows because no later messages are consumed. The same message fails on every attempt (#1728, #1760, #1798), and the resume lines show the offset is stuck at 618947 (#1756, #1794, #1865). The GC pause at #595 is an unrelated early warning. The report-cron pandas failure is a separate deploy issue and does not touch audit-consumer. Alternative considered: resource_exhaustion (stack/heap). Ruled out because the crash is tied to one specific message, not to load or memory growth; the heap was 56% after GC at #595.

verdict.recommendedAction: Quarantine or skip msg-750657 (audit.events offset 618947): move it to a dead-letter queue or advance the consumer's committed offset past it, then restart audit-consumer. Add a guard so expandReferences has a depth limit or cycle detection, and make the consumer dead-letter messages that throw instead of crashing. Inspect the payload of msg-750657 to find out how it was produced. Separately, fix the report-cron:2026.10.2 image, which is missing the pandas module (ModuleNotFoundError), and check whether anything downstream depended on the audit backlog.
